decision_reason: A1 already separates many activity pairs through complementary intensity, timing, posture and translation concepts. Its closest eating and sedentary pairs offer limited grounds for additional reliable IMU distinctions. The principal supported addition is relative wrist-versus-carried-phone motion prominence: it provides a spatial contrast for kicking versus catching and helps distinguish locomotor from wrist-centered activity using seen examples. The low-U_NN dribbling–clapping pair merits attention, but neither bilateral coordination nor ball contact is reliably observable from the supplied inventory, so no dedicated distinction is manufactured. Diagnostic distances guide priorities but do not establish recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_motion_dominance
attributes.definition: Degree to which dynamic motion at the watch-wearing wrist predominates over dynamic motion at the carried phone, assessed only when appreciable activity-related motion is present.

levels.Low: Wrist motion is no more prominent than carried-phone motion, or appreciable activity-related motion is absent.
levels.Medium: Wrist motion moderately predominates over carried-phone motion.
levels.High: Wrist motion strongly predominates while carried-phone motion is comparatively limited.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. It retains transferable contrasts between locomotion, vigorous ball activities and quieter manual tasks, with jogging and catching as vigorous seen anchors. Execution effort and phone carriage can alter magnitude, so intensity alone is not treated as an activity identifier.

cadence: G6 supports repetition-rate evidence from recurring motion cycles. It preserves a useful distinction between dribbling and clapping and transfers through jogging and brushing teeth without equating their movement mechanics. Self-selected pace, pauses and competing wrist/body cycles make intermediate states ambiguous.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes rather than isolated impacts. This preserves the existing eating-sandwich versus eating-soup distinction and separates smoother locomotion from rapidly fluctuating hand actions. Food handling and execution style can blur eating contrasts; no finer utensil-specific attribute is justified.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with footfalls, catches and hand contacts. Catching and jogging provide seen anchors for impulsive unseen activities. Contact need not transmit equally to the watch and phone, and an isolated abrupt voluntary movement can resemble impact evidence.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation in principle. Retaining this concept preserves A1's walking–stairs and sitting–standing contrasts without inventing another posture discriminator. Global inclination is only indirectly observable: phone placement and wrist orientation can disagree with load-bearing body posture, and sitting does not necessarily imply trunk lean.

posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative orientation. It preserves a complementary distinction for kicking versus catching and for walking versus stairs, with folding clothes providing another changing-configuration anchor. Local wrist movement and movement of the carried phone must not automatically be interpreted as global postural change; this limits expected predictability.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular movement at both available devices. The concept transfers from brushing teeth, eating pasta and catching to rotational components of unseen actions. Sensor orientation, joint strategy and whether the instrumented wrist performs the action introduce ambiguity; rotation does not identify a particular joint or manipulated object.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window evidence consistent with progression. Jogging anchors walking and stairs, while stationary manual activities anchor limited progression. Limb translation and phone handling can resemble locomotor motion, and inertial evidence alone does not establish sustained displacement; no vertical-travel dimension is added.

motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal predictability independently of repetition speed. Regular jogging and brushing teeth and more variable catching provide seen support for unseen cyclic and episodic actions. Short windows, deliberate pauses and variable execution can obscure regularity; no reliable improvement over this general concept is established for the close eating pairs.

wrist_motion_dominance: G3 supports comparing dynamic motion prominence at the available watch and phone. Wrist-centered catching and brushing teeth versus distributed jogging supply seen transfer anchors. This adds a spatial contrast to kicking versus catching and to locomotor versus manual activities without requiring observation of the leg or both hands. Expected evidence is appreciable wrist motion with comparatively limited phone motion, rather than merely high total intensity. Predictability is conditional: a hand-carried phone, motion of the uninstrumented hand, arm swing and nearly static windows can undermine the contrast. It is not asserted to separate dribbling from clapping or sandwich from soup.

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes retain distinct physical questions: overall magnitude, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, global orientation change, angular-motion prominence, progression, temporal predictability and relative wrist motion prominence. Smoothness and impulsiveness can covary but distinguish sustained fluctuations from isolated peaks; cadence and regularity distinguish speed from consistency. Wrist motion dominance concerns relative spatial distribution, not absolute intensity or angular motion. The global posture concepts retain substantial placement-related uncertainty. No extra attribute is introduced for bilateral contact, food identity, precise hand trajectories or stair elevation because the supplied capabilities do not establish sufficiently stable independent evidence. Close pairs are allowed to remain close rather than receiving unsupported semantic distinctions.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
